title: 〜ものの
simpleExplanation: 〜ものの means "although (X is true), (Y)". The first part is admitted as a fact; the second part says that things did not go as you would expect from that fact. For example, "I bought the book, but I haven't read it" – buying normally leads to reading, and ものの flags that gap.
whenUsed: Written and formal spoken Japanese (reports, essays, presentations). In casual speech けど / が are used instead. Typical situations: admitting you did something but not the follow-up, or admitting a good point while raising a problem (値段は安いものの、品質が悪い).
formation: な-adjective + な / である + ものの
Noun + である + ものの
Set phrase: とはいうものの (that being said…)

diagram.translation: I bought new shoes, but I haven't worn them even once.

examples.ja: 新しい靴を買ったものの、一度もはいていない。
examples.reading: あたらしいくつをかったものの、いちどもはいていない。
examples.en: I bought new shoes, but I haven't worn them even once.

examples.ja: 大学は卒業したものの、仕事がなかなか見つからない。
examples.reading: だいがくはそつぎょうしたものの、しごとがなかなかみつからない。
examples.en: I graduated from university, but I just can't find a job.

examples.ja: このアパートは駅に近いものの、家賃が高すぎる。
examples.reading: このアパートはえきにちかいものの、やちんがたかすぎる。
examples.en: This apartment is close to the station, but the rent is far too high.

examples.ja: 彼は有名であるものの、実力はそれほどでもない。
examples.reading: かれはゆうめいであるものの、じつりょくはそれほどでもない。
examples.en: He is famous, but his actual ability isn't all that great.
examples.note: な-adjective + である + ものの.

examples.ja: とはいうものの、やはり少し不安だ。
examples.reading: とはいうものの、やはりすこしふあんだ。
examples.en: That being said, I'm still a little worried.
examples.note: Set phrase used to start a sentence.

similarGrammar.difference: Neutral "but". ものの specifically says that the natural consequence did not follow.
"In spite of", stronger surprise or protest. ものの is calmer, an admission of a gap.
"Although", but usually the two parts describe the same subject at the same time (知っていながら).
Formal "although", mainly with verb stems: 知りつつも.

commonMistakes.wrong: 彼は真面目ものの、成績が悪い。
commonMistakes.right: 彼は真面目なものの、成績が悪い。
commonMistakes.why: 真面目 is a な-adjective; it needs な (or である) before ものの, as before a noun.

commonMistakes.wrong: 雨が降ったものの、行きましょう。
commonMistakes.right: 雨が降っていますが、行きましょう。
commonMistakes.why: The clause after ものの must be a statement of fact, not an invitation, command, or request.

commonMistakes.wrong: 値段は安いものの、買った。
commonMistakes.right: 値段は安いので、買った。／値段は安いものの、買わなかった。
commonMistakes.why: ものの needs a result that goes against expectation. Cheap → bought is the expected result, so ものの is wrong.

usageNotes: The second clause often contains なかなか〜ない, まだ〜ていない, or それほど〜ない, expressing an unfulfilled expectation.
ものの is somewhat formal; in speech you will hear 〜けど, 〜のに far more often.
とはいうものの starts a new sentence and means "that said"; it is a common expression in essays.
jlptTips: In 文法形式の判断, ものの is the answer when clause 1 is a completed fact and clause 2 says the natural consequence hasn't happened (まだ / なかなか / 一度も).
Distractors: ものだ, ものなら, ものだから, ものか. Read the following clause: if it is a contrasting fact, choose ものの.
The verb before ものの is usually past or plain; the sentence never ends with a request or volitional form.
